## Tidepool landing page build plan

**1. Navigation**  
A slim, white header with the Tidepool wordmark and a simple wave-shaped icon on the left; “How it works,” “For teams,” and “Pricing” centered; “Log in” and a rounded coral “Try Tidepool” button on the right. Use a friendly geometric sans serif, such as **DM Sans**, in deep navy. Keep the header spacious and sticky on scroll.

**2. Hero**  
Use a two-column layout on a pale seafoam background. Left: a large headline, “Make a week your whole team can see,” a short sentence explaining that Tidepool turns priorities into a shared weekly plan, and two buttons: “Start planning free” and “See how it works.” Right: a crisp product mockup showing a weekly board with tasks, owners, and a few colorful status markers. Add a subtle tide-line illustration behind it. Headline in bold navy; coral highlights one key phrase.

**3. Trust strip**  
A narrow white band with “Made for small teams who do a lot” and four understated customer wordmarks. Keep logos monochrome so the product remains the focus.

**4. The problem and promise**  
On a warm sand background, center the heading “Less chasing. More doing.” Below, use three equal cards for scattered updates, unclear priorities, and overloaded meetings. Pair each with a simple line icon and one brief, empathetic sentence. Close with a line that positions Tidepool as one calm place to agree on the week.

**5. How it works**  
Return to white. Present three numbered steps in a horizontal sequence: gather priorities, make a shared plan, check in as the week shifts. Alternate short copy with small product screenshots. Use seafoam panels, navy labels, and coral step numbers.

**6. Feature spotlight**  
Use a split layout: a large weekly-board screenshot on the left; on the right, explain clear ownership, flexible planning, and lightweight check-ins. Keep copy benefit-led and concise.

**7. Testimonial**  
A full-width deep-navy block with a large seafoam quotation mark, one specific customer quote about fewer status meetings, and the speaker’s name, role, and small portrait.

**8. Final CTA**  
Centered on seafoam: “Give your next week a better starting point.” Include a coral “Plan your first week” button and a no-credit-card reassurance.

**9. Footer**  
White footer with the Tidepool mark, links to product, company, help, and privacy, plus a small “Made for teams finding their rhythm” sign-off.

## Tidepool landing page build plan

**1. Navigation**  
Use a clean white header with the Tidepool wordmark and a small tide-mark icon on the left; “How it works,” “For teams,” and “Pricing” in the center; “Log in” and a coral “Start free” button on the right. Set in **DM Sans**, deep navy **#173B45**. Keep it sticky, compact, and easy to scan.

**2. Hero**  
On a pale seafoam **#EAF6F1** field, pair a strong headline and CTA on the left with a realistic product preview on the right. Headline: **“A calmer way to plan the week together.”** Supporting copy: “Bring priorities, owners, and progress into one shared plan—without adding another meeting.” Buttons: “Start planning free” and a text link, “Take a product tour.” Show a legible weekly board with real-looking tasks, names, and statuses; use coral **#F47762** sparingly for action and emphasis. Avoid decorative imagery that competes with the interface.

**3. Outcome strip**  
A white band with three concise benefits: **“Everyone knows the priority,” “Every task has an owner,” “Plans can change without a scramble.”** Use simple navy line icons and short labels. This replaces unverified customer logos with clear product value.

**4. The before-and-after**  
On warm sand **#F7F2E8**, headline: **“Stop piecing the week together in chat.”** Show two contrasting panels: fragmented notes and messages on the left; a tidy shared plan on the right. Keep the “before” muted and the “after” bright, with copy focused on fewer follow-ups and clearer ownership.

**5. How it works**  
Three numbered steps in a horizontal sequence—**Gather priorities. Agree on the plan. Adjust as you go.** Give each step one sentence and a small, consistent UI crop. Stack vertically on mobile.

**6. Product detail**  
Return to white. Feature a larger board screenshot beside three benefit-led points: shared priorities, visible ownership, lightweight check-ins. Use captions and annotations tied directly to interface elements; don’t claim integrations or capabilities not confirmed.

**7. FAQ**  
Use a simple accordion for practical objections: team size, setup time, pricing, and whether everyone needs an account. Keep answers direct and accurate.

**8. Final CTA and footer**  
Close on seafoam with **“Make next week easier to start.”** Repeat “Start planning free,” plus a brief, verified signup reassurance. Finish with a navy wordmark, product and company links, help, privacy, and terms.
